summary: The new profile-name workflow is mostly defensive, with asserted merge coverage, protected empty-string comparisons, and correct score-before-Jaro-Winkler ordering. The main issue is that the women’s “model first name present” table retains observations classified as cell 4 because of a missing surname, contradicting the report’s description of cell 4 as empty or missing among the names being scored.

findings.title: The women’s model-name-present table labels valid first-name transcriptions as cell 4 missing
findings.what_the_code_does: `hasml` requires only `hm_f` for women: `gen byte hasml = (men & hm_f & hm_l) | (wom & hm_f)`. But inherited `cell==4` means either raw model field is absent because `ml_ok = namefrst_ml!="" & namelast_ml_ditto!=""`. Thus a woman with a usable model first name but no model surname passes the new sample while remaining in cell 4. The generated prose instead says group 4 is “empty or near-empty” and describes it as “missing,” although the women’s table scores only her present first name.
findings.why_it_matters: The new slide-facing table can report a nonzero cell-4 row containing valid model first names and first-name agreement scores, while readers are told that row represents missing model names. This changes the interpretation of both its N and its performance statistics; the uncommitted review artifact reports hundreds of thousands of such observations, but that count could not be independently reproduced here.
findings.how_to_check: In Stata, after constructing `hasml`, run `count if wom & has_dmonth & hasml & cell==4` and `count if wom & has_dmonth & hasml & cell==4 & hm_f`; then tabulate raw surname missingness within that group before dropping `hm_f`/`hm_l`.
findings.suggested_fix: For the women’s first-name table, define a first-name-specific cell classification whose missing category depends only on the model first name, or relabel the existing groups explicitly as full-name cells and state that women in cell 4 can have a present, scored first name but a missing surname.

findings.title: “Ours+Anc” is not constructed with exactly the linkage pipeline’s fallback rule
findings.what_the_code_does: The new table falls back when `strtrim(namefrst_ml)==""` or `strtrim(namelast_ml_ditto)==""`. The linkage construction cited by the prose falls back using the raw tests `namefrst_true==""` and `namelast_true==""`. Whitespace-only model strings therefore use Ancestry in this table but not necessarily in the linkage input; conversely, nonblank punctuation that normalizes to empty is not filled here and receives a zero score.
findings.why_it_matters: If either value pattern exists, the reported “Ours+Anc” statistics do not describe exactly the New transcription used in the linkage tables, contrary to the generated explanation. The size and direction of the numerical difference depend on unseen data.
findings.how_to_check: Before normalization, count raw-nonempty trimmed-empty model fields. After normalization, count trimmed-nonempty fields whose normalized `cf_ml` or `cl_ml` is empty. Recompute the table under raw-empty, trimmed-empty, and normalized-empty fallback rules and compare the means.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one documented rule. Use raw `==""` to reproduce the linkage input exactly, or normalize first and fall back on normalized emptiness if the intended estimand is usable names; revise the generated prose accordingly.

verified_clean.item: Empty strings cannot inflate exact agreement
verified_clean.evidence: The exact full-name and first-name indicators require nonempty normalized source fields at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:132-133.

verified_clean.item: Missing candidate names receive zero rather than accidental positive Jaro-Winkler scores
verified_clean.evidence: `jwpair` excludes empty pairs, asserts scores for eligible pairs, and assigns zero when the candidate is empty at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:71-81.

verified_clean.item: The profile-reference merge cannot silently retain unmatched rows
Women are scored only on first names
verified_clean.evidence: Surname candidates and scores are suppressed for non-men at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:140-144, and the women’s output uses only `xf` and `jf` at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:207-210.

verified_clean.item: The generated text distinguishes agreement from accuracy and discloses the ditto-resolved surname
verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:197 explicitly calls the result agreement with a selected FamilySearch-linked reference, not accuracy, and identifies `namelast_ml_ditto` as ditto-resolved.

verified_clean.item: The master runs the dependent profile-name scripts in the correct order
verified_clean.evidence: `profile_names_score` precedes `profile_names_jw`, with the cache dependency documented, at replication/run_machineA.do:136-148.

verified_clean.item: The newly added frozen input is consistently preflighted and hashed
verified_clean.evidence: The profile dataset is added to the preflight at replication/run_machineA.do:61-64 and to the manifest immediately before the analysis file at replication/hash_inputs.py:75-80, preserving the documented last-file invariant.

verified_clean.item: README preflight counts account for the new input
verified_clean.evidence: The updated counts of 390 inputs, or 391 with `-SkipRebuild`, agree with the added profile dataset at replication/README.md:92-95.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code review was limited to comments, generated report text, and README claims in the working tree.
The external data were unavailable and the Stata pipeline could not be run; affected observation counts and changes in reported means could not be independently measured.
The checked-in MATCHING/results/profile_names_jw.md predates the two newly added model-name-present sections, so their final generated rows were not available for direct inspection.
The untracked prior review reports contain asserted runtime counts, but their underlying data calculation could not be independently verified in this environment.
